behavior: Mostly nocturnal, with activity also around dawn, dusk, and occasionally daytime. Roosts quietly in trees or cavities by day; hunts mainly from a perch, then swoops onto prey, but may also fly low, hover, or take aquatic prey. Territorial pairs communicate with resonant hoots. Diet includes small mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles, fish, crayfish, and invertebrates.
field_marks: Large, stocky owl with a rounded head and no ear tufts
Gray-white facial disc with dark brown eyes and a short yellow hooked bill
Upper breast crossed by horizontal brown bars; lower underparts marked with vertical brown streaks
Brown upperparts mottled and barred with buff-white
Broad, rounded wings and a medium-length rounded tail, both barred brown and pale
Densely feathered legs; feet and talons are often largely concealed while perched
habitat: Large, mature deciduous, mixed, or coniferous forests, especially wooded swamps and forests near water; dense foliage provides daytime roosts, while large trees and cavities provide nest sites.

measurements.weight: 16.6–37.0 oz (470–1,050 g), both sexes; females are generally larger

sources.title: Barred Owl Identification — All About Birds, Cornell Lab of Ornithology
